questions.text: Daniel Burnham's 1905 Plan of Manila incorporated City Beautiful Movement principles. Which of the following was NOT a characteristic of the Burnham Plan?

options.text: Diagonal boulevards radiating from civic centers (e.g., Taft Avenue) creating monumental urban vistas
Large monumental parks and public spaces (e.g., Luneta) serving as civic gathering points and urban landmarks
Mixed-use neighborhoods with informal, unplanned commercial activity and street vending
Grand civic architecture and classical design principles inspired by European and American Beaux-Arts tradition

rationale.a: Diagonal boulevards were signature Burnham elements.
rationale.b: Large parks and civic spaces were core to City Beautiful.
rationale.c: The City Beautiful Movement emphasized formal civic grandeur, not informal mixed-use neighborhoods. Mixed-use walkable neighborhoods are a hallmark of New Urbanism (Palafox era), not City Beautiful (Burnham era).
rationale.d: Monumental classical architecture was fundamental to the movement.
rationale.correct: The City Beautiful Movement emphasized formal civic grandeur, not informal mixed-use neighborhoods. Mixed-use walkable neighborhoods are a hallmark of New Urbanism (Palafox era), not City Beautiful (Burnham era).
rationale.takeaway: Burnham/City Beautiful = formal grandeur. Palafox/New Urbanism = mixed-use walkability (different eras).

questions.text: Why is the evolution from Burnham (1905) to contemporary planners like Palafox significant for understanding Philippine planning history?

options.text: It shows that planning remains unchanged since 1905; modern planners replicate Burnham, which suggests a lack of innovation
It demonstrates the professionalization of planning in the Philippines—from colonial American designs to Filipino-led contemporary practice responsive to Philippine contexts
It proves that Burnham's approach is superior and should still be followed, disregarding modern advancements
It indicates that planning is no longer relevant in modern Philippine cities, which challenges the need for urban planning

rationale.a: Contemporary planners have adapted methods significantly.
rationale.b: The evolution from Burnham's colonial City Beautiful (1905) to Filipino planners (Toledo establishing profession, Palafox applying contemporary methods) reflects the maturation of planning as a Filipino-led, context-responsive discipline. This is a narrative of professionaliza and localization.
rationale.c: Contemporary approaches integrate, not displace, earlier concepts.
rationale.d: Planning remains highly relevant; the evolution shows adaptation.
rationale.correct: The evolution from Burnham's colonial City Beautiful (1905) to Filipino planners (Toledo establishing profession, Palafox applying contemporary methods) reflects the maturation of planning as a Filipino-led, context-responsive discipline. This is a narrative of professionalization and localization.
rationale.takeaway: Planning evolution in Philippines = colonial American → Filipino professional practice, context-responsive.

rationale.correct: Felino Palafox Jr. is the leading contemporary Philippine urban planner. His master plans for Bonifacio Global City and numerous provincial capitals emphasize pedestrian-friendly design, mixed-use development, and strategic growth strategies.

questions.text: What is the significance of Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.'s work in establishing landscape architecture as a recognized profession in the Philippines?

options.text: It separated landscape from architecture; established design standards; integrated landscape into planning
It eliminated the need for urban planners in the Philippines, thereby streamlining the planning process and reducing bureaucratic overhead.
It was focused exclusively on decorative gardening without planning integration, limiting its impact on urban development.
It created a separate government agency for landscape control, which oversees all landscape-related activities and ensures compliance with national standards.

rationale.a: Santos elevated landscape architecture from ornamental gardening to a design discipline integrated with architecture and planning. His work established professional standards and demonstrated how landscape design supports livability, environmental quality, and urban form.
rationale.b: Landscape architecture and urban planning are complementary, not competitive.
rationale.c: Santos's work transcended decoration—it was design discipline and planning integration.
rationale.d: Professionalization occurred through practice standards and recognition, not necessarily new agencies.
rationale.correct: Santos elevated landscape architecture from ornamental gardening to a design discipline integrated with architecture and planning. His work established professional standards and demonstrated how landscape design supports livability, environmental quality, and urban form.
rationale.takeaway: Santos professionalized landscape architecture as integration of design, planning, and environment.

questions.text: If a contemporary Philippine architect-planner aimed to integrate the legacy of Burnham (monumental civic identity), Santos (landscape-integrated design), and Palafox (walkable mixed-use urbanism) in a city planning project, which combination of principles would most effectively achieve this synthesis?

options.text: Replicate only Burnham's diagonal boulevards and civic grandeur; ignore landscape and walkability, focusing solely on monumental aspects
Create grand civic anchors (Burnham) with landscape-integrated corridors (Santos) and pedestrian-focused mixed-use zones (Palafox) that serve community livability
Reject all historical planning; create entirely new, untested approaches that may not align with proven urban design principles
Prioritize car infrastructure over pedestrian or civic space, potentially compromising the project's sustainability goals

rationale.a: Burnham alone ignores community livability and environmental integration.
rationale.b: A synthesis would honor Burnham's civic identity through strategic monuments, integrate Santos's landscape design for environmental livability, and apply Palafox's walkability and mixed-use principles for community function. This creates a layered, historically-informed contemporary design.
rationale.c: Learning from historical precedents strengthens contemporary design.
rationale.d: This contradicts Palafox's walkability emphasis and Santos's ecosystem principles.
rationale.correct: A synthesis would honor Burnham's civic identity through strategic monuments, integrate Santos's landscape design for environmental livability, and apply Palafox's walkability and mixed-use principles for community function. This creates a layered, historically-informed contemporary design.
rationale.takeaway: Synthesis = Burnham's civic identity + Santos's landscape integration + Palafox's walkability.

questions.text: Who designed the 1905 Plan of Manila, and what was the primary urban design philosophy that guided this plan?

options.text: Antonio Toledo; focus on grid-pattern residential neighborhoods with an emphasis on uniformity and predictability in urban layout
Daniel Burnham; City Beautiful Movement with monumental civic spaces and diagonal boulevards
Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.; landscape-integrated planning that prioritizes green spaces and ecological harmony
Felino Palafox Jr.; mixed-use transit-oriented development that encourages sustainable urban growth and reduced reliance on automobiles

rationale.a: Toledo was the first Filipino planner, working in the postwar period (1950s–70s), not 1905.
rationale.b: The 1905 Plan of Manila was designed by American architect Daniel Burnham, who applied City Beautiful Movement principles: grand civic buildings, diagonal boulevards (Taft Avenue), large parks (Luneta), and monumental architecture to elevate civic grandeur.
rationale.c: Santos was a landscape architect/National Artist, not the designer of the 1905 plan.
rationale.d: Palafox is a contemporary planner, not the designer of the 1905 plan.
rationale.correct: The 1905 Plan of Manila was designed by American architect Daniel Burnham, who applied City Beautiful Movement principles: grand civic buildings, diagonal boulevards radiating from civic centers, large parks (Luneta), and monumental architecture to elevate civic grandeur.
rationale.takeaway: 1905 Plan of Manila = Burnham (American) + City Beautiful Movement principles.

questions.text: Compare the planning approaches of Burnham (1905 Plan of Manila) and Felino Palafox Jr. (contemporary BGC master plan). What fundamental philosophical shift is evident?

options.text: Burnham and Palafox share identical approaches; no philosophical shift, as both focus on urban aesthetics
Burnham emphasized monumental civic grandeur and hierarchical space; Palafox emphasizes pedestrian-scale mixed-use walkability and community integration
Burnham focused on community participation; Palafox on top-down government control, reflecting a shift in governance style
Both emphasize industrial zoning and car-dependent sprawl, which remains a constant in urban planning

rationale.b: Burnham (City Beautiful, 1905) used grand civic design and hierarchical spatial organization. Palafox (New Urbanism and contemporary planning) emphasizes human-scale walkability, mixed uses, and community-friendly design. This reflects a shift from monumentalism to livability.
rationale.c: Both value some form of coordination; Palafox emphasizes community participation more explicitly.
rationale.d: Neither emphasized industrial sprawl as primary; Palafox explicitly opposes car-dependent sprawl.
rationale.correct: Burnham (City Beautiful, 1905) used grand civic design and hierarchical spatial organization. Palafox (New Urbanism and contemporary planning) emphasizes human-scale walkability, mixed uses, and community-friendly design. This reflects a shift from monumentalism to livability.
rationale.takeaway: Burnham (1905): monumental grandeur. Palafox (contemporary): pedestrian walkability—philosophical era shift.

questions.text: Who was the first Filipino to establish city planning as a recognized profession distinct from architecture?

options.text: Daniel Burnham, who established planning practice early 1900s
Ildefonso P. Santos Jr., who professionalized landscape architecture
Antonio Toledo, who developed planning frameworks in postwar Philippines
Felino Palafox Jr., who pioneered contemporary planning methodologies

rationale.a: Burnham was American, working in the 1905 colonial period.
rationale.b: Santos professionalized landscape architecture, not planning broadly.
rationale.c: Antonio Toledo was the first Filipino city planner, developing planning frameworks and establishing planning practice as distinct from architecture in the postwar period (1950s–1970s). This professionalization was foundational for modern Philippine planning.
rationale.d: Palafox works in contemporary period; Toledo pioneered the profession earlier.
rationale.correct: Antonio Toledo was the first Filipino city planner, developing planning frameworks and establishing planning practice as distinct from architecture in the postwar period (1950s–1970s). This professionalization was foundational for modern Philippine planning.
rationale.takeaway: Antonio Toledo = first Filipino city planner (postwar era).
